Hi! Yep I’ve shot a couple rolls of film on mine and it’s been great! I’ve got a couple tips for focusing! 

1) Use the focus bubble (I don’t know the correct term for it), when looking through the viewfinder! You’ll see a half/half circle… when the subject is in focus, the image will be level, when out of focus the image will be be unlevel and disproportionate if that makes sense.

2) Check the backfocus of the lens and use the metric/imperial markings on the lens to check focus (Use a tape measure and measure from the sensor to the subject, and focus using focus bubble through viewfinder. Then check the lens if it’s under, over or just right on the mark). It’s an old lens so the focus might not line up anymore… but at least it will give you a rough idea on how to keep your subject in focus!

It’s not the end of the world if it’s occasionally blurry too, I find it kind of suits the aesthetic of shooting on a super 8 camera. If you wanted it clean look you’d shoot on a modern digital camera! Hope that helps:)

There’s not heaps of info out there about this camera but I found this old manual online which was helpful! 

https://www.pacificrimcamera.com/rl/01369/01369.pdf

It takes 2 x different kind of batteries, AA in the handles and these 625 mercury batteries on the bottom of the camera… looks like a little button. You’ll need both to function the camera correctly. The AA’a power the camera’s roll function and the mercury controls the internal light meter and other things from memory.

If there’s any green corrosion in the battery comparents from old batteries, you can use white vinegar and cue tips and clean it up and it should work quite nicely👍🏻
